page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. The server delivers 64 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz via AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 silicon, running one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 512.0 GB of DDR4 system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Hardware features include 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Hardware graphics acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs installed.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput alongside modest single-threaded performance. The server achieves top-quartile results in multi-core stress-ng tests (97,227.26) and cached memory bandwidth reads at 3,792.89 GB/sec. Application benchmarks indicate high throughput in Clang software compilation, static web serving (47.45 GB/sec), and in-memory key-value caching, where Redis SET operations reach 74.12 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects architectural tradeoffs, demonstrating weak performance in single-core Geekbench tests (985.0) and serial compression routines. Large language model text generation also remains weak across all evaluated parameter sizes.

The absence of a virtualization hypervisor eliminates virtualization overhead, delivering predictable access to physical memory channels, non-volatile storage, and physical compute cores. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the density of the Graviton2 core layout, the large 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage. Amazon Web Services r6gd.metal is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis and Memcached deployments, relational databases with high IOPS requirements, and large-scale continuous integration compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 64-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz on arm64 architecture. Equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it offers an 8.0 GB per core ratio along with 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline networking. Without hypervisor contention or GPU accelerators, the instance delivers dedicated physical execution with strong multi-threaded scaling, high cached memory bandwidth, and 74.12 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution and AI generation benchmarks remain modest, its extensive memory array and integrated high-speed local storage provide balanced performance for in-memory databases, key-value stores, relational database engines, and software compilation clusters.
